ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Streetlights in cities, the power supply lines of trolleybuses, etc., are often suspended using triangular structures. The figure shows a simplified model of this type of structure: the left end of a rigid rod can rotate without friction about an axis passing through point B and perpendicular to the plane of the paper; the right end, point O, is suspended from point A by a steel cable. The weights of the steel cable and the rigid rod can both be ignored. A heavy object of constant mass is suspended at point O. Now the steel cable is slowly shortened, and the suspension point A of the steel cable is slowly moved downward, so as to ensure that the rigid rod is always horizontal. Then during the above process, which of the following statements is correct? ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The pulling force exerted by the steel cable on point O becomes larger

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Streetlights in cities, the power supply lines of trolleybuses, etc., are often suspended using triangular structures. The figure is a simplified model of this type of structure: the left end of a rigid rod can rotate without friction about an axis passing through point B and perpendicular to the plane of the paper; the right end, point O, is suspended from point A by a steel cable. The weights of the steel cable and the rigid rod can both be ignored. A heavy object of constant mass is suspended at point O. Now the steel cable is slowly shortened, and the suspension point A of the steel cable is slowly moved downward, so as to ensure that the rigid rod is always horizontal. Question: During the above process, how does the pulling force exerted by the steel cable on point O change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The pulling force exerted by the steel cable on point O becomes larger
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, on the left side there is a vertical support line, point A is above, and point B is below it; the rigid rod extends horizontally to the right from point B to point O; the steel cable connects obliquely downward from point A to point O; a heavy object is suspended below point O. Reasoning: Let the angle between the steel cable AO and the horizontal rigid rod BO be θ. The weights of the steel cable and the rigid rod are ignored, the mass of the heavy object is constant, and the process is slow, so any instant can be regarded as static equilibrium. Taking moments about point B, the heavy object produces a clockwise moment mg·BO at point O; the vertical component T sinθ of the cable tension T at point O produces an opposite moment, while the horizontal component is along the direction of the rod and has zero moment about point B. Therefore the equilibrium condition is (T sinθ)·BO = mg·BO, namely T sinθ = mg. The rigid rod is always horizontal and the length BO is constant; when the steel cable becomes shorter and point A moves downward, the vertical height of A relative to B decreases, so the angle θ between the steel cable and the horizontal rod decreases, and sinθ also decreases. Since mg is unchanged, from T = mg/sinθ it can be known that T increases.
